title: New major hospital, Brisbane: structure
workplace: New major hospital with a hospital tower, two level basement and rooftop helipad, Brisbane
note: Facts are example inputs for testing. On a real project they come from the contractor's own procedures and the project's documents.

swms.title: Formwork, reo and post-tensioned slabs
swms.task: Form, reinforce and pour the post-tensioned floor slabs of the hospital, working on formwork decks more than 2 m above the floor below, with concrete placed by a boom pump.

facts.fallControl: Edge protection is installed around every open deck edge before work starts, and no one works outside it.
facts.controlsConsidered: Edge protection was considered for every task, and an elevating work platform where edge protection cannot be fixed.
facts.formworkDesign: Formwork and falsework are to the engineer's design FW-210 (revision B), checked and signed off by the formwork engineer before each pour.
facts.loadLimits: Loads are placed only in the areas marked on the structural engineer's drawing S-402 (3 kPa), checked by the site engineer before loading starts.
facts.systemInstructions: The formwork system is erected to the supplier's instructions (document FS-2, revision 4) by a crew trained by the supplier.

steps: Install edge protection and lay the deck
Load ply onto the deck while it is being laid
Set up the concrete pump and placing boom

swms.title: Stressing the post-tensioned slabs
swms.task: Stress the post-tensioning tendons on each floor slab of the hospital once the concrete reaches the engineer's strength, grout the ducts and cut the tendon tails. Stressing is done at the slab edge, more than 2 m above the floor below.

facts.fallControl: Stressing is done from inside the perimeter screens, which stay in place until stressing is complete.
facts.controlsConsidered: Edge protection was considered for every task, and an elevating work platform where edge protection cannot be fixed.
facts.stressingProcedure: Stressing follows the post-tensioning engineer's sequence on drawing PT-200, once cylinder tests show the strength the engineer requires. The post-tensioning subcontractor's trained crew does the stressing. Exclusion zones behind each jack and along the tendon line are barricaded and signed.
